messages:
maria: Running a small-GPU VPC perf run on the new private infra. Enabling batch-slicing for continuous batching and saw tail latency spikes (~95th/99th) when concurrent short requests land in the same slice. Posting a small summary and logs.

kevin: Can you paste the config you used? was token budget lowered for the VPC knobs?

maria: Config snippet I used:```
private.batching.enabled=true
private.batching.slice_enabled=true
private.batching.slice_threshold=0.18  # fraction of seq len to cut into slices
private.batching.max_token_budget=1500
private.batching.short_priority=true
private.kernel.prefer_fused=false  # force fallback for now
```

akiko: Interesting — prefer_fused=false will force some models onto the generic kernel path, which can increase per-token latency on small GPUs. Did you run with KV cache warm?

maria: KV cache warm but we saw cache churn on multi-tenant host: sometimes cached shards were evicted when other tenants spiked. I added a quick trace: `kv_cache.misses: 0.27` during the spike window.

samir: Two quick hypotheses: 1) slice_threshold too low => many slices => overhead + kernel launch cost. 2) short requests queueing with long ones in same slice causing padding waste and de-optimizing kernel selection.

kevin: Agree. On constrained hardware we often want to bias batching toward token-budget targets instead of count-based batches. Try increasing `max_token_budget` to 2048 and set `slice_threshold=0.3` so we don't over-slice. Also flip `prefer_fused=true` to pick optimized kernels where possible.

maria: Will try. Also saw perf-bot flamegraph for a run where spike happens: `https://perf.internal/runs/1849/flame` — main hotspots are `batch_assemble()` and `kernel_dispatch_generic()`

perf-bot: Automated profile summary for run 1849: assemble_time p95=42ms, kernel_dispatch_generic p95=58ms, kv_lookup p95=12ms. Suggestion: prefer_fused kernel reduces dispatch p95 by ~30% on similar hardware.

akiko: Another knob: queue policy. If we set `queue.short_first=true` we prefer flushing short requests earlier; reduces tail for short-interactive flows. But that can increase latency for very long contextual generations. Need workload-dependent tradeoff.

samir: We should add an override path for Private/VPC that sets more conservative defaults for small GPUs:
```
private.defaults.small_gpu = {
  max_token_budget: 2048,
  slice_threshold: 0.3,
  prefer_fused: true,
  queue_policy: "short_first",
  kv_reserve_ratio: 0.15  # reserve some KV mem to avoid eviction churn
}
```

maria: Ran with those overrides — immediately saw 95th drop ~18ms in smoke tests. Need longer soak to ensure no regression under high concurrency.

kevin: Can you add an A/B canary: 10% of instances with new defaults, 90% baseline? Also record `batch_size_histogram` and `slice_count_histogram` for a week.

maria: On it. I'll push canary tomorrow and attach dashboards. TL;DR: slice heuristics + kernel choice + KV reservation fixed the main tail for small VPC hosts in initial runs.

akiko: Nice. Follow-up: add an experiment to try token-budget-aware batch formation (prefer grouping by tokens not just count) — that should reduce padding waste.

samir: Filed a tracking ticket: INF-4321 "Small VPC: slice/budget defaults & token-aware batch formation".

maria: Thanks all. Will post results once the canary runs 24h. :thumbsup:
